title: Exclusive | Nous Research Scores $90 Million to Bring Open-Source AI Assistant to Enterprises
source_used: Ventureburn write-up of the round (does not name the WSJ). WSJ blocked (401, paywall). WSJ credit from its own headline in Google News and from CryptoRank and Dealroom headlines.
key_facts: Nous Research secured $90 million in a Series B round to build enterprise versions of its Hermes AI agent (Ventureburn).
The round took the valuation to $1.5 billion; investors named by Ventureburn are Nvidia, Microsoft's M12, Samsung, Robot Ventures, Union Square Ventures and Y Combinator.
Hermes for Businesses lets companies run AI models locally or in the cloud, so their data stays with them (Ventureburn).
CEO Dillon Rolnick says $90 million is modest by current AI funding standards and that the team works with less (Ventureburn).
Ventureburn cites Hermes usage figures (24 million clones and about 2.5% of global token usage, by internal estimates); these are not checked here.
WSJ headline (7 Oct 2026, Google News): the company's round at a $1.5 billion valuation was reported by the WSJ.
quote_evidence: Nous Research secured $90M to build enterprise-grade versions of its popular AI agent, Hermes.
Its latest funding round has pushed the valuation of the startup to $1.5 billion.
It allows businesses to run highly capable AI models locally or in the cloud.
why_it_matters_hint: A funded open-source option for companies that want to keep their data in-house.
notes: WSJ 401 here. Text read in Ventureburn's write-up. Ventureburn does not name the WSJ; the WSJ credit comes from its headline and from CryptoRank and Dealroom headlines that cite the WSJ for the valuation. Company-side usage claims left out of the summary.
